hooks.command: IN=$(cat); if [ -n "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-}" ]; then printf %s "$IN" | uv run --with 'mcp<2' python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/directive_recall.py"; fi

IN=$(cat); if [ -n "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-}" ] && printf %s "$IN" | python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/directive_prefilter.py"; then printf %s "$IN" | uv run --with 'mcp<2' python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/directive_recall.py"; fi

hooks.statusMessage: MemHub: checking directives for this failure
hooks.command: IN=$(cat); if [ -n "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-}" ] && printf %s "$IN" | python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/reactive_prefilter.py"; then printf %s "$IN" | uv run --with 'mcp<2' python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/directive_recall.py"; fi

IN=$(cat); case "$IN" in *git*commit*|*"gh pr"*) if [ -z "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-}" ]; then echo "[memhub-flush] CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT unset; cannot locate flush scripts, skipping" >&2; elif printf %s "$IN" | python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/flush_prefilter.py"; then printf %s "$IN" | uv run --with 'mcp<2' python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/flush_session.py"; fi ;; esac

hooks.statusMessage: MemHub: PR created — arming babysit loop
hooks.command: IN=$(cat); case "$IN" in *gh*pr*create*) if [ -n "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-}" ]; then printf %s "$IN" | python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/pr_babysit_trigger.py"; fi ;; esac

IN=$(cat); if [ -n "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-}" ] && printf %s "$IN" | python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/turn_flush_prefilter.py"; then printf %s "$IN" | uv run --with 'mcp<2' python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/flush_turn.py"; fi

hooks.prompt:
You are a silent SessionEnd hook for MemHub. Your job is to save this Claude Code session into MemHub team memory, then exit. The hook input available to you includes `transcript_path` (this session's .jsonl file), `session_id`, and `cwd`.

Steps:
1. Read the file at `transcript_path`. It is JSONL — one JSON object per line.
2. Parse every line into a JSON object, preserving order, to get the full ordered list of transcript records.
3. Identify the MemHub MCP tool whose name ends in `__import_conversation` — a plugin install exposes it fully qualified, as `mcp__plugin_memhub_memhub__import_conversation` (production) or `mcp__plugin_memhub-staging_memhub__import_conversation` (staging). Pick whichever one is actually present in your tool list; do not assume an unqualified `mcp__memhub__import_conversation` exists. Note which of the two you found — step 4 needs it.
4. Resolve the repo's room (agent brain) so this session lands in team memory rather than personal memory:
   - Derive the repo's room NAME from its remote: run `git -C <cwd> remote get-url origin`, strip the transport/host and any trailing `.git`, keep the last two path segments, and prefix with `Repo: ` — e.g. `git@github.com:XTraceAI/xmem.git` becomes `Repo: XTraceAI/xmem`. Preserve case exactly. Not a git repo, or no `origin` remote → skip to step 5 with no room.
   - Read `~/.config/memhub-plugin/rooms.json`. Missing or unparseable → skip to step 5 with no room; this is an ordinary state (the repo has not been onboarded), NOT an error to report.
   - Look up `repos[<that name>]`, then take `.production.brain_id` if the tool you found in step 3 was the `memhub` one, or `.staging.brain_id` if it was the `memhub-staging` one. Never fall back to the other backend's entry — the two hold different ids and a cross-write silently lands in the wrong brain.
5. Call the tool from step 3 with:
   - `messages`: that list of raw transcript records, passed through AS-IS (do not summarize, filter, edit, or reshape them — the tool auto-detects the Claude Code shape and runs agentic, tool-aware extraction).
   - `conversation_id`: the `session_id` from the hook input (so re-runs of the same session dedup instead of duplicating).
   - `source_platform`: "claude".
   - `agent_brain_id`: the brain id from step 4. OMIT this argument entirely when no room resolved — do not pass null or a guessed id.
   - `namespace`: the repo name resolved by running `git remote get-url origin` in the session's working directory (basename without `.git`, e.g. "VecDB-Backend"). Omit it if there is no git remote — never guess from a directory name.
6. Use ONLY that MCP tool. Never use curl, fetch, or any direct HTTP call.
7. Produce no user-facing output — this runs in the background.

If the memhub MCP server is not connected/authenticated, the tool is unavailable, or the call returns an error, do not raise and do not print to the user — but DO leave a breadcrumb, because a silent exit here is indistinguishable from a successful capture and loses the whole session with no signal. Append one line to `~/.config/memhub-plugin/session-capture.log` (create the directory if needed) in the form `<ISO-8601 UTC timestamp> session=<session_id> SKIPPED: <one-line reason>`, then exit 0. Write the same breadcrumb with `OK: <n> records -> <room brain id or "personal">` on success.
